author.name: Søren Kierkegaard
author.heading: About Søren Kierkegaard
author.bio: Søren Kierkegaard explored faith, anxiety, choice and the difficulty of becoming a self, often through pseudonymous voices. The Sickness unto Death appeared under the name Anti-Climacus and treats despair as a problem in a person’s relation to the self and to God.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: What began as a theological analysis became a compact lesson in authenticity as it passed through humanistic psychology and later popular writing. Rogers read Kierkegaard as describing the responsibility of choosing to be oneself; Sasportas condensed that interpretation, and subsequent quotation books made it look like a sentence lifted directly from Kierkegaard.
